extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners (PTAB/Federal Circuit litigators and patent prosecutors)
extracted.subtask_description: A compilation of 2022 PTAB, district court, ITC, and Federal Circuit decisions and PTAB precedential/terse guidance summarizing legal standards and practical rules for practice before the PTAB and related forums.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standing to appeal IPR decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioner can have standing to appeal an adverse IPR even if it was not sued so long as there is a realistic risk of suit (e.g., Patent Owner sued a customer, no covenant not to sue, petitioner still selling products to that customer and others).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court found standing where petitioner sold relevant products to affected customers and Patent Owner did not offer covenant not to sue; presence of possible direct or indirect infringement suits supports standing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim construction: ordinary meaning and context
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim terms should receive their ordinary meaning based on interpretation of the entire claim in context, not by isolating a single element.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Court cautioned that 'it is not always appropriate to break down a phrase and give it an interpretation that is merely the sum of its parts.' Use intrinsic evidence to interpret terms in context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motivation to combine/obviousness requires 'how' and 'why'
rubrics_metrics.description: To show motivation to combine references, petitioner must adequately explain the 'how' and 'why' a person of ordinary skill would combine the teachings as proposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where petitioner explained how and why combinations worked, substantial evidence supported Board findings of motivation to combine; absent such explanation, Board may be affirmed for lack of motivation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Means-plus-function and indefiniteness: Board must evaluate structure in specification
rubrics_metrics.description: When means-plus-function issues arise, the Board must decide for itself whether required structure is present in the specification and whether absence of such structure precludes resolving prior-art challenges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A party's assertion of indefiniteness does not automatically relieve the Board from determining whether structure exists; indefiniteness that makes resolution of prior-art impossible may affect estoppel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert testimony: witness must have ordinary skill to opine as POSITA
rubrics_metrics.description: An expert offered to testify from the perspective of a skilled artisan must have at least ordinary skill in the art; without that, opinions are neither relevant nor reliable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied in claim construction, validity, and infringement contexts; lack of ordinary skill can render expert testimony inadmissible for POSITA-perspective issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant-Admitted Prior Art (AAPA) is not a patent or printed publication
rubrics_metrics.description: AAPA is a binding admission by a patentee regarding scope and content of prior art but is not itself a patent or printed publication and therefore cannot by itself form the 'basis' of an IPR ground under §311(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a ground relies in part on AAPA, the Board must assess whether AAPA improperly formed the basis of the ground; later Director guidance clarified that AAPA used in combination with a patent may not be the basis if the patent forms the basis and AAPA fills missing limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption of nexus for objective evidence of nonobviousness
rubrics_metrics.description: A presumption of nexus between objective evidence of nonobviousness and the claimed invention applies if the patentee shows the product is essentially the claimed invention and that the presumption is coextensive with claimed features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Products having unclaimed features do not automatically defeat presumption if such features are insignificant; challenger cannot rebut by argument alone and must present evidence that the objective evidence was due to extraneous factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forum selection clauses can preclude IPRs
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may contractually bargain away the right to file IPR petitions through unambiguous forum selection or waiver clauses directing validity disputes to a district court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts will enforce unambiguous contractual promises not to file IPRs, rejecting public-interest/fairness objections if clause is clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estoppel applies to simultaneously filed IPR petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: When a petitioner files multiple IPRs on the same day against overlapping claims and final written decisions are issued in some, estoppel under §315(e)(1) can bar maintenance of remaining IPRs addressing the same claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioner could have consolidated petitions under §315(d) to avoid separate FWDs that trigger estoppel; knowledge of grounds at filing time is relevant to estoppel.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPR estoppel covers all grounds reasonably could have been raised
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutory IPR estoppel (§315(e)(2)) precludes a petitioner, after receiving a final written decision, from later raising in district court any ground that was raised or reasonably could have been raised in its IPR petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This principle follows from Caltech v. Broadcom and supersedes prior narrower readings that tied estoppel only to instituted grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: District court review available for denials based on IPR estoppel in reexaminations
rubrics_metrics.description: Although statutory reexamination denial for lack of substantial new question is non-reviewable, denials based on IPR estoppel (which post-date reexamination statute) may be subject to district court APA review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alarm.com v. Hirshfeld held district courts can review denials premised on IPR estoppel because such estoppel did not exist when reexamination statute was enacted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Venue under 28 U.S.C. §1400(b): 'regular and established place of business' requires control and presence
rubrics_metrics.description: To establish venue based on a 'regular and established place of business' of a defendant, a plaintiff must show regular physical presence of an employee or agent conducting the defendant's business with principal-level control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independent dealerships/franchisees with limited constraints typically do not suffice absent evidence of the defendant's right to control their operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obviousness: combination disclosures can support obviousness
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim limitation disclosed only by combining references can still render the claim obvious if a POSITA would have been motivated to combine and there is substantial evidence that combining would yield the claimed limitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court emphasized POSITA's 'knowledge, creativity, and common sense' in combining teachings; the fact that only the combination discloses the limitation does not defeat obviousness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board should not ordinarily find substitute claims unpatentable on sua sponte grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed substitute claims should rarely be found unpatentable by the Board on sua sponte grounds; the record must 'readily and persuasively establish' unpatentability for such sua sponte action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: POP reversed a sua sponte finding where record did not convincingly support that substitute claims were unpatentable for same reasons as original claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry skepticism is a secondary consideration in obviousness and must be invention-specific
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence of general industry skepticism about a field does not necessarily defeat motivation to combine; any skepticism must be specific to the claimed invention and combination, not generic to the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vague or generic testimony that a field was skeptical is insufficient; remand may be required for Board to weigh specific evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB vacating institution partly as a sanction is generally unreviewable
rubrics_metrics.description: A panel's decision to vacate an earlier institution decision that also serves as a sanction may be unappealable in certain circumstances (lack of jurisdiction to review the Board's decision to vacate institution in part as sanction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court held it lacked jurisdiction to review certain vacaturs where the institution determination was deemed unreviewable; dissent may view as appealable sanctions order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printed publication availability and inventor contribution burden
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner bears the burden of persuasion to show a purported printed publication author made an inventive contribution such that the reference constitutes 'by others' prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court required assessment of corroborating evidence (co-authoring, role, related patents) and remanded where Board's credibility findings were untenable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointments Clause: temporary inferior officer may constitutionally perform Director functions
rubrics_metrics.description: An inferior officer temporarily performing the USPTO Director's functions can constitutionally review PTAB decisions when acting in the limited period between Directors, under the Appointments Clause and the FVRA's scope on non-delegable duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court held such temporary action constitutional because rehearing requests are delegable duties and the Vacancies Reform Act did not bar the temporary review in that context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definiteness: ambiguous terms may be definite if intrinsic record provides reasonable certainty
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if a term (e.g., 'self-similar') is susceptible to more than one meaning, it is not necessarily indefinite if the written description, with reasonable certainty, provides the term's scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court credited Board's factual finding that the term had a well-known meaning and examples in the specification supported definiteness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obvious error in prior art disclosures (In re Yale standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a prior art reference includes an obvious typographical or similar error apparent to a POSITA who would mentally disregard the errant information, that errant information does not disclose the subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantial evidence may support Board finding that data in a table was an obvious error, but whether an error is 'obvious' may be contested (dissent may disagree).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue cannot recapture subject matter deliberately surrendered during prosecution (recapture rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reissue is available only to correct inadvertent mistakes; a deliberate narrowing to overcome a §101 rejection cannot be corrected via reissue to recapture surrendered subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court affirmed that the recapture rule applies to amendments made to avoid §101 rejections just as it does for prior-art-related amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forfeiture of untimeliness challenges on appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: A Board finding that a theory was untimely is an independent ground for affirmance; appellants must challenge untimeliness on appeal or forfeit that argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if the Board reached the merits, failure to challenge an untimeliness ruling in the opening brief forfeits that issue and leaves the untimeliness holding as an independent basis for decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product-by-process limitations give no patentable weight if they do not change structure
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'cast in one piece' (product-by-process) limitation imparts no patentable weight if it is not shown to impart a structural difference from products not cast in one piece.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims construed as product-by-process limitations may fail to distinguish over prior art if no structural difference is demonstrated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estoppel can apply to grounds denied institution under prior partial-institution practice
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner may be estopped from later asserting grounds that were denied institution pre-SAS if those grounds were included in the petition because 'it is the petition, not the institution decision, that defines the scope of the IPR.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioner may have been able to seek a SAS remand but failing to do so may lead to estoppel in later litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's discretionary power to review institution denials (Arthrex context)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Arthrex, the Director must have the discretion to review PTAB decisions; institution decisions remain committed to the Director's unreviewable discretion but the Director retains review authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal Circuit read Arthrex to confirm that the Director's authority to review exists and that mandamus is generally unavailable where Director discretion is implicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent eligibility §101: claims directed to abstract mental processes are ineligible
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims directed to abstract processes that essentially perform steps in the human mind (e.g., determining Social Security Disability Insurance benefits via a computer network framed as an abstract idea) are patent-ineligible under §101.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board applied abstract-idea analysis and found essential steps were performed in the human mind; §101 rejections under Alice/Mayo framework supported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fintiv discretionary-denial factors (and Director June 2022 Interim Guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may deny institution based on discretionary Fintiv factors, considering (inter alia) likelihood of district court trial date occurring before the Board issues final written decision, extent of district-court investment, overlap and stipulations addressing duplication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director's June 2022 Interim Guidance clarifies application of Fintiv factors; courts/Board weigh factor 2 (trial timing), factor 3 (investments in litigation), factor 4 (stipulations/overlap), and whether petition presents a compelling challenge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compelling evidence standard can overcome prior jury verdict to support institution on remand
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Director's Interim Guidance, if a petition presents 'compelling evidence of unpatentability' the Board should not discretionarily deny institution based on a prior jury verdict rejecting validity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board may institute on remand if at least one prior art reference was not before the jury or other compelling reasons support strengthening patent system by reconsidering validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Plastic framework does not automatically apply to prior reexaminations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board declined to extend the General Plastic discretionary-denial framework to prior inter partes reexamination proceedings; prior reexamination alone is not dispositive for denying IPR institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board will consider differences in challenges between reexamination and IPR and will not mechanically apply General Plastic factors to reexaminations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design-patent IPR challenges must address differences between prior art and claimed design
rubrics_metrics.description: For design-patent obviousness grounds, petitioner must adequately address differences between the prior art and the claimed design and explain how the primary reference would be modified; otherwise grounds are inadequate for institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to provide adequate obviousness analysis (particularity, how references modify claimed design) can lead to denial of institution, especially where an anticipation ground is the only viable ground.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ranking of parallel petitions is recommended but not always required
rubrics_metrics.description: Trial Practice Guide advises petitioners to provide a ranking of parallel petitions, but the Board may decline to deny for failure to rank if other factors (e.g., no claim overlap, district-court claim count) weigh in favor of institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board has discretion to excuse failure to rank where practical circumstances make ranking infeasible or unnecessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Draft/unfiled declarations are protected work product and not discoverable
rubrics_metrics.description: Unfiled draft declarations that would expose an attorney's mental impressions or litigation strategy are presumptively protected work product and not discoverable under PTAB discovery rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board distinguished discoverable 'facts and data' from protected mental impressions; inadvertent reliance on a draft in deposition does not necessarily waive protection if the declarant did not file it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board may deny institution as inefficient use when only a single claim likely to prevail
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may exercise discretion to deny IPR institution when a petition challenges many claims but establishes a reasonable likelihood of prevailing for only a single claim, making institution an inefficient use of resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board relied on prior informative decisions (e.g., Chevron Oronite, Deeper) to deny institution when only one of many challenges has a plausible chance of success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second petitions can be instituted despite substantial overlap when new facts arise
rubrics_metrics.description: A later-filed petition that substantially overlaps an earlier petition may still be instituted if intervening facts (e.g., new priority-date allegations by Patent Owner) justify reconsideration and petitioner lacked reason to presume earlier priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board will consider factors outside General Plastic when circumstances changed such that the second petition raises materially different issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redundant or overlapping grounds are not per se disqualifying if adequately particularized
rubrics_metrics.description: Some overlap among grounds may be permissible; petitions are acceptable if grounds are not excessive, are explained, and petitioner identifies which references are relied upon for each limitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board will evaluate whether grounds meet §312(a)(3) particularity and whether a POSITA would have combined teachings with a reasonable expectation of success; unexplained redundancy can be a basis for denial.
